newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Eskom, unions to meet again next Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Eskom, unions to meet again next Tuesday.

text.p: A follow-up meeting aimed at bringing South Africa's labour movement back on board the process of restructuring electricity utility Eskom will be held on January 14, a Public Enterprises Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

Government, Eskom management and representatives of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) and the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (Numsa) met on Tuesday to discuss the unions' withdrawal last week from a committee dealing with Eskom's restructuring -- the Restructuring and Transformation Committee.
Wandile Zote, spokesman for Public Enterprise Minister Stella Sigcau, said the meeting on Tuesday had agreed to discuss problems raised by the unions last week.

"It is in the interests of both Eskom and the two unions NUM and NUMSA to revisit the internal relationship with Eskom with regard to the problems raised by the unions," government, labour and Eskom management said in a joint statement.
NUM and Numsa withdrew from the committee last week because of concerns in four areas:
- a planned outsourcing deal between Eskom and IBM on information technology
- an internal regrouping of management within Eskom
- the possible sales of mothballed power stations or recommissioning of decommissioned plants
- the structuring of the electricity distribution sector.

"We have agreed to have a follow-up meeting that will evaluate progress made in the restrucuring and transformation committee thus far and highlight the issues where there has been agreement, deal with issues of disagreement within the RTC and areas where there is lack of clarity."
Zote said government was concerned that the privatisation process might be delayed unnecessarily.
"For this process to have any credibility we will have to have union participation," he added.
President Nelson Mandela's government has committed itself to the privatisation or restructuring of state corporations but progress to date has been slow.
The first major sale of state assets is expected in the next three months with the planned sale of up to 30 percent in telecommunications group Telkom.
